context: José's ruling D-HIST-01-1 = B with note: use original datasets rather than AddBiomechanics; add AddBiomechanics predicted-GRF column only if obtainable without the full download.
method: Read-only web/metadata work, 2026-10-31. No full archive, original-data file or B3D file other than one 503,665-byte zip member was downloaded.

AddBiomechanics archive: HEAD, single and two-range GETs; zip64 tail and full central directory (331,662 B) re-read by HTTP Range and parsed independently; sha256 equals the HIST-01 value 88d494cc...ce09.

One B3D: train/No_Arm/Tiziana2019_Formatted_No_Arm/Subject29/Subject29.b3d (smallest non-empty member) range-fetched (503,665 B compressed), CRC32 verified, then only the header protobuf parsed with a minimal wire decoder; frames were not decoded.
Official dataset Google Drive tree (download-page redirect) listed from public folder pages only; one 1 KiB range and one two-range request against the same Subject29 file on Drive.
Originals: SimTK project and download pages, GroundLink page and HEAD requests, Zenodo/figshare/DataCite APIs, author README, PubMed, web search.

grf_premise.question: Are AddBiomechanics ground reaction forces predicted, or processed measured force-plate data?
grf_premise.answer: Processed measured force-plate data. No predicted GRF is part of the AddBiomechanics 1.0 release.

evidence.claim: Released frames contain measured ground reaction forces and moments from force plates.
evidence.quote: Each of these frames contains optical marker locations and ground reaction moment and force measurements ... Each raw data source includes experimental optical motion capture and force plate data
evidence.source: https://addbiomechanics.org/download_data.html (also Werling K, et al. AddBiomechanics Dataset: Capturing the Physics of Human Motion at Scale. ECCV 2024, doi:10.1007/978-3-031-73223-2_27; arXiv:2406.18537 (read via https://ar5iv.arxiv.org/html/2406.18537), section 3)
evidence.quote_check: Download-page wording checked in the saved page (sha256 7dcb3f20...c791); the ECCV section-3 match was read via an automated web reader.

evidence.claim: The B3D keeps raw plate readings and, per processing pass, plate data assigned to contact bodies.
evidence.quote: raw_force_plate_*: "the raw force plate readings, per force plate, without any assignment to feet or any post-processing"; ground_contact_center_of_pressure/torque/force: "the original force-plate data in world space, one per ground contact body"

evidence.claim: Plate loads are assigned to the feet and the measured forces and centers of pressure are inputs, not optimization variables.
evidence.quote: "We assign loads from each force plate to the feet in the model based on when the feet are penetrating the ground"; "Since the ground reaction forces are known from experimental data"; "the center of pressure locations are fixed based on the ground reaction force data"
evidence.source: Werling K, et al. AddBiomechanics: Automating model scaling, inverse kinematics, and inverse dynamics from human motion data through sequential optimization. PLoS ONE 18(11):e0295152, 2023, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0295152
evidence.quote_check: Quote extracted by an automated web reader from the publisher HTML / ar5iv rendering; not re-checked against the PDF.

evidence.claim: Per-pass copies may be filtered: pass headers carry low-pass cutoff/order and per-plate background-noise cutoffs; an acceleration-minimizing pass type has a force regularization weight.
Frames without trustworthy GRF are kept and flagged per frame, not filled with predictions.
evidence.quote: missingGRFReason: "the reason that this frame is missing GRF, or else ... notMissingGRF to indicate that this frame has physics. WARNING: If this is true, you can't trust the tau or acc values on this frame!!" Enum includes notOverForcePlate, interpolatedClippedGRF, shiftGRF, manualReview, footContactDetectedButNoForce.

evidence.claim: Measured example: Subject29 (Tiziana2019) has one trial of 64 frames; 16 frames notMissingGRF, 48 flagged (43 manualReview, 3 footContactDetectedButNoForce, 2 missingBlip). Contact bodies calcn_r, calcn_l; passes kinematics, lowPassFilter, dynamics.
GRF prediction appears only as a benchmark task with baseline models in the dataset paper, not as released data.
evidence.quote: section 5 benchmark "estimating physical forces from an observed movement"; baselines in section 5.3
evidence.source: Werling K, et al. AddBiomechanics Dataset: Capturing the Physics of Human Motion at Scale. ECCV 2024, doi:10.1007/978-3-031-73223-2_27; arXiv:2406.18537 (read via https://ar5iv.arxiv.org/html/2406.18537)
evidence.quote_check: Quote extracted by an automated web reader from the publisher HTML / ar5iv rendering; not re-checked against the PDF.

grf_premise.likely_source_of_extra_rows: The legacy LocoHub files were not written by the current converter. The two earlier converters, the consolidated script at commit cc94be4 (contributor_tools/conversion_scripts/AddBiomechanics/convert_addbiomechanics_to_parquet.py at cc94be4, line 140 'ss = frame.processingPasses[1]  # Use dynamics processing pass', records appended once per frame near line 317) and contributor_tools/conversion_scripts/AddBiomechanics/_archive/b3d_to_parquet.py (line 116 'ss = a.processingPasses[1]'), each write one row per frame from processingPasses[1]. cc94be4 also substitutes 70.0 kg when the subject mass is unavailable (line 287); the _archive script reads getMassKg() with no fallback (lines 272-278). Per-pass row expansion therefore cannot explain extra rows in the legacy files. Plausible remaining cause, unverified against legacy files (not local): frames whose GRF is flagged (e.g. off the force plates) are kept in the B3D and were written as rows (Subject29: 48 of 64 frames flagged); trials are also split into segments by GRF availability and at most 20 s ('AddBiomechanics will automatically crop trials into different segments depending on the time points that have ground reaction force data', https://addbiomechanics.org/faq.html).
grf_premise.consequence: Where the original dataset includes force plates (9 of 11; Tan walking only as stance windows), the AddBiomechanics GRF would duplicate measured GRF already in the original, after AddBiomechanics foot assignment and filtering. It is not an independent predicted channel.
grf_premise.current_converter_rows: The current source-preservation adapter (convert_addbiomechanics_to_parquet.py at HEAD, lines 104-106) writes one raw-frame row plus one row per processing pass for every frame (1 + P rows; 4 for a 3-pass trial), with JSON source payloads, and keeps flagged frames. It produced none of the legacy files. This matters for any future AddBiomechanics rebuild (D-HIST-03-1 option C).

archive_host.member_access: Yes: any single member can be fetched by range from its local header offset (Subject29: local header 30+65+28 B at 257476763268, payload 503,665 B at 257476763391).
archive_host.limitation: B3D members are deflate-compressed (method 8; 1,085 of 2,335 entries). Deflate is sequential, so no frame can be decoded without all compressed bytes before it; a 64 KiB prefix of Subject29 expanded to 1,428,033 B, less than its 3,103,603-B header. GRF-only from the zip therefore requires the whole member.

per_subject_b3d.host: Google Drive folder linked by https://addbiomechanics.org/redirect/main_dataset_download.html -> https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1X3OEJXF5gzvjR5vRG7VO7h58bRwYTV0a ("addb_dataset_publication": test|train / No_Arm|With_Arm / study / subject / .b3d)
per_subject_b3d.single_range: 206, Content-Range bytes 0-1023/3605883 for Subject29.b3d; the 1 KiB equals the expanded zip member prefix
per_subject_b3d.note: Drive download quotas and throttling were not tested. The AddBiomechanics docs ask users not to re-download from their servers repeatedly (AWS cost); that request concerns the app, but repeated per-frame requests would be the same kind of load.

b3d_layout.layout: int64 little-endian header length, SubjectOnDiskHeader protobuf, then fixed-size frame records in trial order; each record = one sensor frame (markers, IMU, EMG, raw plate force/CoP/torque) followed by one frame per processing pass (pos, vel, acc, tau, ground-contact wrench/CoP/torque/force, COM, root-frame copies).
b3d_layout.source: https://github.com/keenon/nimblephysics/blob/c405b056fc35068027e03e0c384e84e12870b475/dart/proto/SubjectOnDisk.proto; https://github.com/keenon/nimblephysics/blob/c405b056fc35068027e03e0c384e84e12870b475/dart/biomechanics/SubjectOnDisk.cpp (read: lines 308-365; write: lines 415-500; readFrames seek: lines 960-1060)

measured.header_content: mostly OpenSim model text per pass (SubjectOnDiskPass.model_osim_text)

b3d_layout.grf_bytes_basis: Schema arithmetic for 2 contact bodies: wrench 12 doubles, CoP/torque/force 6 doubles each, plus 2-B tag+length per packed field; frames not decoded.
b3d_layout.can_read_grf_without_rest: Only in principle and only from the uncompressed Drive files: header + one byte range per frame (GRF fields are interleaved in every frame record, and Drive refuses multi-range requests). That is about one HTTP request per frame, of order 10^7 requests for these 11 studies (estimate), so not practical. From the zip it is impossible without the whole member.

grf_only_feasibility.practical_route: Stream one No_Arm member at a time from the archive by range, extract GRF, delete the member. Transfer equals the full compressed member bytes; peak disk equals the largest member (1.64 GB, ta21); retained data is the GRF fields only (about 3% of frame bytes by the Subject29 layout).
grf_only_feasibility.verdict: GRF cannot in practice be obtained without transferring each needed subject's full B3D bytes. It does not require the whole 417.7 GB archive, the With_Arm variant, or keeping any B3D on disk. Because the GRF is measured plate data and not a prediction, it adds nothing for studies whose original data include force plates.

legacy_pass_index_note.finding: Both legacy converters read processingPasses[1], commented as the dynamics pass. In Tiziana2019 Subject29 the trial's pass order is [kinematics, lowPassFilter, dynamics], so index 1 is the low-pass-filter pass, which per the nimblephysics docs filters the kinematics pass output before the dynamics pass. Legacy joint angles, moments and GRF may therefore come from a pre-dynamics pass for such subjects. Checked on one subject only; pass order in other subjects and whether that pass's tau/GRF equal the dynamics pass were not checked.

option_c_output_estimate.rows_per_frame_current_converter: 1 + P (P = processing passes per trial; 3 in the one subject read)
option_c_output_estimate.basis: Frame count is an order-of-magnitude estimate from the Subject29 frame size applied to each study's expanded No_Arm bytes; P = 3 assumed for every trial.
option_c_output_estimate.output_bytes: not estimated: depends on the JSON payload size per row and Parquet compression, neither measured
option_c_output_estimate.converter_change: None assumed. Fewer rows (one pass per frame, flagged frames kept or dropped) would need a converter change, which is not proposed here.
